title: MCP — Registry
description: Registry reloads and multi-instance hash consistency. The divergence panels read the SAME recording rules that back the alerts in alerts.yaml (mcp:registry_hashes:count) rather than recomputing the expression — a dashboard computing its own version would eventually disagree with the alert, and that disagreement surfaces as 'the graph looks fine' during an incident.

panels.title: Distinct registry hashes — must be 1
panels.description: All instances of one deployment compile the same configuration, so they must all report the same hash. 2 or more means pods are answering tools/list differently and an agent's view depends on load-balancer luck. Requires the mcp:registry_hashes:count recording rule from alerts.yaml to be loaded.

panels.title: Divergence over time
panels.description: A brief excursion to 2 during a rolling update is EXPECTED and is why the alerts debounce for 5m. A line that stays above 1 past that window is a real configuration bug — different overlays reached different pods.

panels.title: Instances per hash
panels.description: The panel that tells you WHICH failure you have. One instance disagreeing with fifty is a pod that failed to roll; an even split is a half-applied config change. Same detection, opposite responses — and this is how you tell them apart without writing a query at 3am. The legend shows each hash in DECIMAL, because the recording rule builds it with count_values from the value of mcp_registry_hash_id rather than from a label (a hash label would add a permanent series per reload — #136). Convert with printf '%013x' to get the prefix /mcp/health/ready reports; you rarely need to, since this panel is about the SHAPE of the split.

panels.title: Operations in the live registry by instance
panels.description: Operation count per pod. Two instances reporting different counts is the concrete shape of the divergence — it is literally a different tool surface per pod. Broken down by `instance` rather than by registry hash since #136: the hash was a metric label with an unbounded value set, adding a permanent series on every reload, while `instance` is a scrape label bounded by the size of the deployment. Which hash each pod serves is answered by the divergence panels above, which read the mcp:registry_hashes:count recording rule — that rule is computed from mcp_registry_hash_id, a separate single-series gauge carrying the hash as its VALUE, so identity survived the label's removal.

panels.title: Reload rate by outcome
panels.description: Registry reloads and how they ended. error_class splits a benign superseded reload — one reload overtaken by a newer one, which is normal under rapid config churn — from a real failure.

panels.title: Failed reloads (24h)
panels.description: A failed reload leaves the instance serving its PREVIOUS snapshot — it does not crash and it does not go unready. So a pod can sit on stale configuration indefinitely while looking perfectly healthy, and this counter plus the divergence panel above are the only places that shows.
